info.name: My Collection
info.description:
### Welcome to Postman! This is your first collection. 

Collections are your starting point for building and testing APIs. You can use this one to:

• Group related requests
• Test your API in real-world scenarios
• Document and share your requests

Update the name and overview whenever you’re ready to make it yours.

[Learn more about Postman Collections.](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collections/collections-overview/)

item.name: OpenWeather - Weather

request.description:
This is a GET request and it is used to "get" data from an endpoint. There is no request body for a GET request, but you can use query parameters to help specify the resource you want data on (e.g., in this request, we have `id=1`).

A successful GET response will have a `200 OK` status, and should include some kind of response body - for example, HTML web content or JSON data.

item.description:
This folder contains requests for interacting with the **OpenWeatherMap API**.

Currently, it includes:

- **Openweather - GET for city** — Retrieves current weather data for a specified city using the OpenWeatherMap `/data/2.5/weather` endpoint. The request uses the `{{API_Key_OpenWeather}}` environment variable for authentication and returns results in **metric units** (°C, m/s). A basic test is included to verify that the response returns a `200 OK` status code.

item.name: OpenWeather - Forecast
item.description: Contains requests for retrieving 5-day weather forecast data from the OpenWeather API. Requests query the `/data/2.5/forecast` endpoint using a city name and return 3-hour interval forecast entries covering temperature, weather conditions, wind, humidity, and cloud cover. It covers the forecast for a period of 5 days. Results are returned in metric units and authenticated via the `API_Key_OpenWeather` environment variable.
